title: File Descriptor Leak in Loops (Undropped Handles)
pattern: Opening file descriptors, sockets, or process pipes inside iteration loops and bypassing standard RAII drop behavior (e.g., using `std::mem::forget`, leaking references, or passing to an unbounded global collection).
why_bad: Systems enforce strict file descriptor limits per process (e.g., standard POSIX limits of 1024) [394]. Bypassing standard resource cleanup in loop contexts triggers file descriptor leaks, causing subsequent calls to `open()`, `accept()`, or socket creation to fail with EMFILE ("Too many open files") errors and crashing process capability [357, 394, 547].
detection: Identify calls to file or socket open methods inside a loop that are passed to `std::mem::forget` or collected into a vector that is never drained.
fix: Ensure resource handles are safely scoped so they are dropped and closed immediately after use, or close files explicitly [547].
source: Brendan Gregg, *Systems Performance*, Chapter 2 & Chapter 13 / passages [357, 394]; [2nd] Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer*, Chapter 33 / passage [547].
